body.p: Ebuilds are sourced and executed by bash, in an environment that the package manager controls. This section describes the properties of that environment which ebuilds may rely on.
Ebuilds and eclasses may use the features of the bash version that their EAPI guarantees:
body.important: Do not use features of a newer bash version than the EAPI allows, even if the bash installed on your system supports them. Doing so will break on systems with an older bash. Note also that the package manager sets bash's compatibility level to the version listed above, so behaviour that has changed between bash versions will follow the older version.

body.p: The global scope of an ebuild (and of any eclasses it inherits) is executed every time the ebuild is sourced. This includes metadata generation, which may happen on a different machine and without any of the ebuild's dependencies installed. See for the resulting requirement of metadata invariance.
When being sourced, an ebuild must not do any of the following:

ul.li: Call external programs, including via command substitution
Write anything to standard output or standard error
Modify the state of the system in any way

body.p: Bash builtins and the package manager functions that are documented as callable in global scope, like has or ver_cut, are fine:
body.codesample:
# DO NOT DO THIS! MY_PV=$(echo ${PV} | tr . _)
# Do this instead MY_PV=$(ver_rs 1- _)

body.p: Whether variables defined at the top level of an ebuild or eclass are evaluated in global scope or as if within a function body is unspecified, and ebuilds must not rely on either behaviour. Therefore, at the top level:

ul.li: The local builtin must not be used
The declare builtin must only be used with the -g option when defining variables

body.codesample:
# DO NOT DO THIS! declare -A MY_MODULES=( [foo]=1.0 [bar]=2.1 )
# Do this instead declare -gA MY_MODULES=( [foo]=1.0 [bar]=2.1 )

body.p: For characters in the ASCII range, case modification and collation order (LC_CTYPE and LC_COLLATE) are guaranteed to behave as in the C locale. Ebuilds can therefore rely on bash constructs like ${var^^} or on the sorting order of glob expansion, without having to set these variables themselves.
body.note: This guarantee covers the ebuild environment only. External commands that generate output which the ebuild parses may still be affected by the user's locale.

body.p: The ENV_UNSET variable holds a whitespace delimited list of variables that the package manager removes from the environment before sourcing an ebuild. It is set in profiles and in make.conf, not in ebuilds.

Its purpose is to keep variables from the calling user's environment from leaking into builds and changing their outcome. The profiles use it for variables such as the XDG_* directory settings, which are meaningless for a build and regularly break one when they are inherited from a running desktop session.
body.note: Ebuilds must not rely on ENV_UNSET to protect them. If a build is sensitive to some variable, unset or override it in the ebuild itself.

body.p: The failglob option of bash is set in the global scope of ebuilds. As a consequence, a pattern that matches no file results in an error when the ebuild is being sourced, instead of being silently left as a literal string.

body.note: failglob is only set while the ebuild is being sourced, i.e. in global scope. It does not apply inside phase functions.
